curriculum.lesson_evidence: Timbre is the tone colour that lets you tell sound-makers apart when pitch and duration match. This lesson uses four families you can hear in a house: voice, wood, metal, and skin. Voice carries breath and a vowel or hum. Wood often gives a dry knock that stops quickly. Metal often rings after the hit. Skin, meaning a stretched surface such as a balloon or your own thigh, gives a dull thud. Identify the family from the sound description. Do not use brand names, logos, or a picture of a shop instrument. Timbre matters because two notes can share a pitch and still be different music.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Sort these described sounds into voice, wood, metal, or skin, and name one clue for each: a whispered "mmm", two pencils tapped together, a bunch of keys shaken once, and a palm pat on your thigh. What family is each sound?

FEEDBACK
A strong answer matches whisper to voice, pencils to wood, keys to metal, and the thigh pat to skin, with a clue that is about the sound rather than a product name. The whisper has breath and no ring. The pencils knock and stop. The keys jangle and shimmer. The thigh thud is soft and dull. If two answers share a family, the clues must still explain why. A brand or a shop label is not a clue you can hear.

WATCH FOR
If two sounds are both short knocks, they have the same timbre, so wood and metal belong in one family. That fails because a wooden knock usually stops dead while a metal knock leaves a ring. The length of the ring is a timbre clue even when the hits are equally short. Listen past the attack and describe what remains.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Name the family and one heard clue for each new sound: you sing the word "noon", you knock a wooden door, you tap a metal lid with a fork, and you drum two fingers on a balloon. Do not reuse the chair, the pot, the pencils, or the keys. Write four lines, with no brand names. If a lid does not ring, say what you actually heard and choose the family that matches that sound.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.
